# Changelog

## 2.5.1 — 2026-11-02

- **Documentation only - no code changes:** Added Simplified Chinese (README.zh.md) and Spanish (README.es.md) translations of the README and of the v2.5.0 deep-dive notes (docs/v2.5.0-deep-dive.zh.md, docs/v2.5.0-deep-dive.es.md); all four language editions are cross-linked in the README navigation line, and the npm package now ships all four languages. Suite unchanged: 277 tests (275 passing, 2 skipped).

## 2.5.0 — 2026-11-02

- **Consequence targeting - friction lands on contributors, not bystanders (`src/tier2-active/cusum-tripwire.ts`, `herd-detector.ts`, `enforcement-tiering.ts`):** Added `consequenceTargets(snapshot)` partitioning a CUSUM campaign snapshot into friction targets (members with net in-cohort LLR contribution > 0, minus protected members), protected members, and non-contributing members, so hosts enroll step-up only on the members who produced the evidence. `HerdFlagSnapshot` now carries `memberCoverage` and `memberUniqueCoverage` (records served by exactly that one member inside the group), computed at flag time, and `herdFrictionTargets(snapshot)` in `enforcement-tiering.ts` returns the members whose unique coverage is material against the new constant `HERD_FRICTION_MIN_UNIQUE_RECORDS` (25 - under 1/12 of the herd flag's 300-record coverage floor, so a member below it cannot have materially driven the flag; snapshots without the field fall back to all members). A lawful campaign ceiling is deliberately NOT targeted this way: it caps the cohort's total extraction over ALL serves, including non-contributors' - a data cap, not a per-subject punishment - and `checkServe` still passes protected subjects through individually. Classic evidence (2.5.0 classic round, protected side): in the combined control instance, the polite user and all 5 NAT users standing inside a flagged herd group were skipped with `uniqueCoverage` 0 while friction landed exactly on the 3 systematic-review seats (the 2.4.0 round enrolled the whole group); a new dedicated bystander cell - polite users browsing mid-session while an undeclared review team triggered the flags in the same group - measured 0 enrollments, 0 dwell, 0 session expiries, 0 step-downs and 0 rejections for the bystanders.
- **CUSUM cohort formation for the two blind shapes (`src/tier2-active/cusum-tripwire.ts`):** New `formation` options on the tripwire (all host-tunable, on by default). Served-set complementarity forms cohorts from filtered list traffic: a text filter has no honest ordinal-range predicate, so adjacency could never see slicers - but the exact served set is always known, and co-active identities whose served sets are disjoint (Jaccard <= 0.10), individually past the tiling member gate (150) with a pairwise union >= 300, now merge. Cold-walk complementarity forms cohorts on the detail channel: identities whose COLD fetches (ids never introduced to them by a list) tile disjoint, range-dense (>= 0.5) ID ranges inside a co-activity window merge at the same union floor; warm fetches contribute nothing. Singleton scores are still discarded at merge, solo walkers still never form a cohort, and the systematic-review shape still forms and crosses identically to a walker team (consequences remain friction-capped for inferred cohorts; the protected lane is unaffected) - all stated in the module header. `CusumDecision` now also exposes per-stream `bins` (the raw observable label each stream used), so offline calibration tooling reads observables, not just increments. Classic evidence: the slicing crew produced its first CUSUM crossing at union 1,700 (11 members) and the ID walk at union 900 (6 members) - both shapes had 0 crossings in the 2.4.0 round. Unit evidence in `tests/consequence-formation.test.cjs` (11 tests), including the separation checks: scattered support deep-linking (range density ~0.01) does not merge, warm readers do not merge, a solo 800-record walker never flags.
- **Offline calibration fit (`scripts/fit-cusum-calibration.cjs`):** New deterministic script (seeded PRNG) that generates labeled traces for 10 lab-simulated persona families (6 legit, 4 attacker; 60 traces, 40,932 events), replays them through the tripwire, fits per-stream LLR tables by leave-one-family-out with Laplace smoothing and a [-3, 3] clamp, fits N_eff from legit cohort union growth (500 on this set), and evaluates false positives/negatives on the held-out families. It emits the opt-in tables `scripts/r7-labfit-1.tables.json` (load via `options.llrTables`) and a sample manifest `scripts/r7-labfit-1.manifest.json` whose attester is explicitly "lab-simulated" and which evaluates to the **step_down** tier (holdout FP 0.167 exceeds the ceiling floor and sample sizes are below the ceiling minimums). Holdout comparison: r7 fold-fit FP 6/36 vs r6-calib-1 FP 18/36 (the fix lands on the NAT-group and onboarding families; the review-team family still crosses under both), FN 6/24 for both (the time-staggered dispersed family is missed by both), median attacker detection union 1,175 vs 1,225. Because r7 does not beat r6 on BOTH sides, the SDK default stays `r6-calib-1` per the pre-registered rule; the script's proposal says so. Known fit gap: no lab attacker family emits range predicates, so the fitted adjacency table is all zeros and the adjacency stream is inert under r7. Harness trial cell with r7 wired in: polite+NAT controls produced zero flags and zero consequences (r6 shows a below-floor telemetry crossing there), and the ID walk crossed later than under r6 (union 1,350 vs 900) with identical headline extraction (the run is herd-dominated; token lower bound ~989,389 vs ~989,402).
- **Hard-ceiling classic cell - lawful path exercised end-to-end, exactness gap recorded, NOT retuned away:** A dedicated harness instance declared the attacker cohort (`declaredCohorts`), supplied a ceiling-tier calibration manifest (labeled test attestation) and a declared ceiling of 600 records, with `checkServe` wired into the serving path. The lawful path fired for the first time: cohorts crossed into `campaign_engaged`, `ceilingActive` latched, and from engagement onward the cap was absolute - 0 records served to declared identities after the first refusal, 720 `campaign_ceiling` refusals, and the controls in the same instance (polite user + declared-protected compliance) were completely unaffected (1,200/1,200 records, zero friction). But the pre-registered exact-stop line FAILED: engagement is crossing-gated, and at script speed each cohort's union had already reached ~900 records when its score crossed, so the 18 declared identities extracted 2,700 records in total against the declared 600. The gap is recorded in `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` (a declared ceiling bounds a crossed cohort's total, with overshoot equal to the union at crossing); no threshold was adjusted at that stage to make the cell pass.
- **Declared campaign ceiling ARMED at declaration - the exact-stop gap above is fixed (`src/tier2-active/cusum-tripwire.ts`):** A host-declared cohort backed by a ceiling-tier calibration manifest no longer waits for a crossing: declared groups form one cohort at tripwire construction, the ceiling is armed from declaration (`ceilingActive` plus the new snapshot field `ceilingArmed`; decisions also carry `ceilingActive`), the union counts from the first record served, and `checkServe` enforces the cap with no crossing and no consequence floor - including capping a multi-record request at the remaining headroom so request granularity cannot overshoot, and covering single-member declared groups. A declared cohort without a ceiling-tier manifest arms nothing (no armed hard lock; the crossing-time tiering clamp is unchanged), inferred cohorts keep the crossing-gated path exactly as before, and the protected-cohort registry remains a separate lane that neither arms nor disarms a declared cohort. Classic re-test (protected side, pre-registered exact-600 line, two runs on the final build): the declared cohort's union stopped at EXACTLY 600 distinct records in both runs (was 2,700), all 18 walkers blocked, 710 and 714 `campaign_ceiling` refusals, 0 records served past the cap, and controls in the same instance unaffected (compliance 1,200/1,200, zero friction instance-wide); the declared-protected compliance cell (i) also re-ran at 1,200/1,200 with zero friction on both runs. Residual limits - the check-then-serve concurrency gap (exactness is proven for the sequential single-process wiring; atomicity under concurrent serves belongs to the transactional ledger's reservation), one declared size and one attacker shape measured, and mid-process manifest expiry not disarming an armed cohort - are stated in `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`. Unit evidence in `tests/declared-ceiling.test.cjs` (7 tests).
- **Coverage-complete herd grouping (`src/tier2-active/herd-detector.ts`):** Two changes close the grouping gap the previous classic round measured (the slicing herd's flag only ever consequenced the 8 of 18 phase-1 identities who were present and material at first crossing). (1) The coverage-complement linking is now **leader-based**: an identity's coverage group is compared against other groups' aggregates (a refcount map plus a 128-byte block bitmap per group) instead of against every other identity, the scan is throttled per identity by a single growth scalar, and no per-pair state is kept (`maxPairEntries` is accepted and ignored, deprecated). The merge test is the lab complementarity test applied to the two aggregates, so two singleton groups behave exactly as the old pairwise test did. Measured on the same bench both ways: the pairwise design needed 131.3 s for a 1,000-identity x 60-record stream (21.9 ms/event); the leader design processes it in 1.55 s, merges a 500-identity complementary stream into one group in 2.73 s, and handles 2,000 identities x 60 records in 6.2 s. (2) A flagged group now **re-announces itself**: groups track each member's unique coverage at its last announcement, and when a late joiner or a pending partial contributor crosses the materiality floor (`lateJoinerMinUniqueRecords`, default 25 - the `HERD_FRICTION_MIN_UNIQUE_RECORDS` derivation), a supplementary flag (new optional `supplementary: true` on `HerdFlagSnapshot`) fires, coalesced by `supplementaryCooldownMs` (default 5,000) to at most one per group per window - a burst of crossings is announced together, never one flag per member, and nobody crossing inside the window is lost, only delayed by at most the window. A member announced at exactly zero unique coverage is settled-inactive and never re-triggers on its own (documented contract in the module header and LIMITATIONS). Classic evidence (2.5.0 round): slicing A - one herd flag naming all 18 phase-1 identities, 17 step-up enrolled, 16 stepped down, flagged-or-consequenced **18/18** (previously 8/18), phase 1 still 78% and 25 identities / ~19 min overall; ID walk B - phase 1 held to exactly **9,000 = 90.0%** with all 18 walkers capped at the 500-record soft floor and 324 phase-1 interrupts (previously 91.0%, 224 interrupts, 2 walkers escaped to 556/548). The sub-90% remainder is the tiering law's floor, not a grouping miss: an inferred cohort cannot lawfully be cut below 500 per member (18 x 500 / 10,000 = 90.0%); going lower needs a host-declared cohort or a ceiling-tier manifest. All four control cells re-measured at their established lines (declared compliance 1,200/1,200 with zero friction; undeclared 1,200/1,200 with zero data loss and the baseline graduated friction, byte-identical to the earlier runs in this round; polite+NAT and bystander zero consequences). Unit evidence in `tests/herd-phase3.test.cjs` (6 tests).
- **Canary-echo ids (`src/tier2-active/canary-echo.ts`, NEW; exported from `src/index.ts`):** `mintEchoId(secret, { mintedFor, scope?, ttlMs? })` issues a signed synthetic reference id - `echo_<payload>.<sig>`, HMAC-SHA256 over a versioned payload carrying the minted-for identity, optional scope, a 128-bit random nonce per mint, issued-at and expiry (24 h default) - so an echo id is unforgeable without the server secret and cannot be enumerated from another id. `verifyEchoId()` distinguishes malformed / bad-signature / expired / scope-mismatch failures without echoing payload claims back; `resolveEchoFrom()` returns the minted-for identity (or undefined) for the host's tripwire feed; `isEchoId()` and the constants `ECHO_ID_PREFIX` / `DEFAULT_ECHO_TTL_MS` complete the surface. Embedding helpers follow the canary pattern: `mintEchoRecord()` returns a synthetic record for list/record surfaces and `canaryEchoLink()` a hidden `rel="nofollow"` trap link. The intended wiring is one line at the host's record route: resolve the presented id and, when it names a different identity, feed `CusumEvent.echoFrom` - the two identities merge into one cohort at the touch. Classic evidence (2.5.0 round, env-gated harness wiring): a fresh rotation identity presenting the origin identity's echo id was cohort-merged **at the touch, with 0 records served of its own** (cohort exactly {origin, rotation}, union 355 = the origin's served set), and the merged cohort crossed ~0.9 s later at 1,392 union records with both members contributing and both step-up enrolled. An echo touch is a correlation signal, not proof of malice; the payload is integrity-protected, not confidential. Unit evidence in `tests/canary-echo.test.cjs` (7 tests), including the tripwire merge below the 150-record formation gate (where the echo is the only possible link), forged-echo and self-echo negatives.
- **Attacker economics, 2.5.0 classic round (protected side, scripted drivers, single runs per cell):** REA-style rotation stopped at 5.0% (500/10,000 records, token lower bound ~64,449). Slicing still completed via rotation, but phase 1 (18 identities) was held to 78.0% over ~19 minutes with 25 identities overall, and after the grouping fix the herd flag/consequence set covered all 18 phase-1 identities (8 of 18 before it). ID walk still completed: phase 1 held to exactly 90.0% - the inferred-cohort soft floor of 500 records per member - with 324 phase-1 session interrupts and every walker capped (before the grouping fix: 91.0%, 224 interrupts, 2 walkers over the floor). Controls: declared compliance 1,200/1,200 with zero friction; undeclared compliance 1,200/1,200 with friction (3 step-up enrollments, 33 session expiries, 3 soft step-downs) and zero data loss; polite+NAT and bystander cells zero consequences.
- **Docs:** README (EN + VI) refreshed to latest-only - 277 automated tests (275 passing, 2 skipped), the 2.5.0 classic-round numbers above, the shared-ceiling row keeps the CEILINGFIX measurements (exactly 600, twice; 710-714 refusals) - and the calibration-pilot section integrated in both languages. `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` records the implemented leader design with its measured scale bound, the supplementary semantics (including the settled-inactive contract), and a new canary-echo row with its honest bounds.
- **Suite:** 277 tests (275 pass, 0 fail, 2 pre-existing RSA-PSS skips), up from 246 in 2.4.0.

## 2.4.0 — 2026-11-02

- **Transactional disclosure ledger + shared campaign ceiling (`src/tier2-active/disclosure-ledger.ts`):** Added `createDisclosureLedger()` with `reserveDisclosure()` as the single atomic enforcement point for a cohort-wide ceiling over the exact union of served records. The store contract splits honesty classes per the overnight SDK review (CHATGPT-R8: "no enforcement without a transaction"): a store implementing `transactLedger(ledgerId, expectedVersion, updater)` - CAS on `ledgerVersion` covering the union bitmap, reservations, ceiling, rate bucket and evidence accumulators in one transaction - runs `mode: "enforce"`; a get/put-only store runs `mode: "audit_only"` with `enforced: false` on every decision, and the module never claims the ceiling under concurrency it cannot guarantee. The bundled `createInMemoryTransactionalStore()` serializes transactions per ledger (an `ioDelayMs` option simulates a slow backend inside the transaction); a shipped conformance test runs 40 parallel reservations against that slow store and proves exactly the 100-record ceiling is reserved, never more. Reservations count against the ceiling while open and are bounded per CHATGPT-R8 (TTL 60s default, max 2 outstanding and 500 reserved records per subject, optional host-set cohort outstanding cap, lazy + eager expiry, idempotency keys, and a separate host-authorized long-reservation path for slow exports); re-delivery of already-committed records is free. A declared cohort registry fails closed for unregistered subjects by default (the lab's round-6 partial-registry failure, in product form), with `checkRegistryCompleteness()` reporting missing members and an explicit `audit_only` unregistered policy as opt-out. `mergeCohortBucketStates()` encodes the round-6 min-merge rule (merged cohort buckets never reset upward). Unit evidence in `tests/disclosure-ledger.test.cjs` (16 tests).
- **Sequential evidence engine - mixture GLR-CUSUM tripwire (`src/tier2-active/cusum-tripwire.ts`):** Added `createCusumTripwire()` implementing CUSUM-SPEC: four streams (predicate adjacency with gap <= 0.015 / IoU < 0.10 edges, exact-set disjoint tiling with evaluation gates, cold-ID misses over exact introduced sets with stride regularity, cursor-velocity EWMA) emitting LLR increments from versioned lookup tables into one one-sided accumulator per cohort (zero floor - no innocence banking - boundary `B = ln(1/alpha)`, default alpha 1e-3). Tiling conditionally EXCLUDES records inside ranges that already formed adjacency edges, so the two partition views are not double-counted. Cohort formation is adjacency components plus canary-echo links; singleton scores are discarded at merge (documented v1 simplification); bucket state min-merges on component merge; whole-domain predicates form no edges (the round-6 polite-user contamination fix). Crossing latches a per-epoch flag and, in `enforce` mode, engages the shared ceiling + cohort bucket ONLY when the tiering law allows. The default mode is `enforce` (revised 2026-11-02, see the default-law bullet below): an eligible crossing enrolls step-up friction and cohort pacing with no host opt-in - but only at the step-up tier, because the bundled tables remain uncalibrated; `observe` remains available for telemetry-only deployments. Host-declared protected subjects (below) keep the evidence but never the consequence: their decisions stay `logged` (`protectedSubject: true`), snapshots list them under `protectedMembers`, and `checkServe` passes them through. A crossing must also clear a consequence floor before it may carry ANY consequence (step-up enrollment, cohort pacing): the cohort's exact union coverage must reach `consequences.minUnionRecords` distinct records, defaulting to the tiling stream's per-member evaluation gate (150) - the spec's one absolute-scale constant, reused so the two cannot drift apart. The floor is a fix for the v2.4 classic test's one red-line failure (a polite+NAT cohort crossed at a union of 25 records and step-up dwell landed on a legitimate user): below the floor the flag is telemetry only - score, snapshot and `onCampaignFlag` all stand - while eligibility is evaluated live, so a flagged cohort that grows past the floor becomes eligible without a new crossing. Snapshots and decisions carry `consequenceEligible` / `consequenceFloorRecords`, and snapshots add `contributingMembers` (members whose net in-cohort LLR contribution is > 0) so hosts enroll the members who actually produced the evidence. The bundled tables are `r6-calib-1`, fitted on scripted lab traces (N_eff = 189), and ship labeled `uncalibrated: true` with the notice "uncalibrated - audit only" on every snapshot - no effectiveness percentage is claimed. Unit evidence in `tests/cusum-tripwire.test.cjs` (14 tests), including the conditional-LLR exclusion, the whole-domain guard, and the consequence floor (below-floor polite+NAT shape is telemetry-only with zero friction, campaign-scale crossing still enrolls step-up, floor is host-configurable).
- **Enforcement tiering law + calibration manifests (`src/tier2-active/enforcement-tiering.ts`, `calibration-manifest.ts`):** Added `clampEnforcement()` / `maxEnforcementAction()` encoding the rule approved after the R5 lab failure (a priced `graduated_only` band hard-cut a simulated compliance team at 551/1,200 records): inferred cohorts (herd detector, CUSUM) cap at the friction tier (below); hard ceilings require a host-declared cohort or ceiling-tier calibrated evidence; `deny` additionally requires ceiling-tier calibration on a host-declared cohort. `herdBandPrice()` is 0 for both bands, and `validateHerdResponseConfig()` rejects any configuration attaching a price, budget override or channel multiplier to the `graduated_only` band, so the R5 wiring mistake fails at startup. `evaluateCalibrationManifest()` replaces boolean calibration gates with a tiered manifest (model version, calibration version, holdout sample sizes and FP/FN rates, method, attester, issued/expiry): absent, incomplete or expired manifests evaluate to `audit_only`, complete ones to `step_down`, and only manifests meeting stricter error floors and sample minimums reach `ceiling`. Unit evidence in `tests/reviewer-tiering.test.cjs` and `tests/attribution-calibration.test.cjs`.
- **Default-on friction + protected cohorts - the 09:44 default-law revision (`src/tier2-active/enforcement-tiering.ts`, `src/tier2-active/protected-cohorts.ts`):** The tiering law's DEFAULT flipped (Danny, 2026-11-02 09:44): the one measured systematic-review team is rare in practice and is a declared activity in real organizations (audits are scheduled, pentests run under rules of engagement), so protection moves to an explicit declaration and enforcement turns on by default. Inferred cohorts now cap at the **friction tier**: step-up plus a SOFT budget step-down bounded below by `SOFT_BUDGET_FLOOR_RECORDS` (500 distinct records - derived from the disclosure ledger's shipped per-subject reservation bound, the largest single bulk unit one subject may hold; also the R5 prototype's override value, whose lethality came from the 5x cold-fetch multiplier stacked on it, not from the number). `softBudgetStepDown()` computes the lawful result (a demand to cut an inferred cohort to zero returns the floor, never 0), `clampEnforcement()` reports the floor as `budgetFloorRecords`, and `defaultHerdBandResponse()` maps BOTH herd bands to friction for inferred cohorts - the ladder's deep cut now requires a host-declared cohort or a ceiling-tier manifest, and `applyHerdLadder()` still refuses `graduated_only` outright. Hard ceilings, below-floor cuts and cold pricing remain code-forbidden for inferred cohorts even when configuration demands them. New `createProtectedCohortRegistry()`: hosts declare compliance/audit/support/pentest subjects (with reason and optional expiry); protected subjects accrue full telemetry but receive zero inferred-evidence consequences - the CUSUM tripwire takes the registry's `isProtected`, and host-side handlers partition target lists via `partitionConsequenceTargets()` / `guardInferredConsequence()`. Protection does not cover host-authorized consequences or direct per-subject evidence (a protected subject's own decoy hit still taints it). Unit evidence in `tests/default-law.test.cjs` (9 tests: defaults bite with no opt-in, hard demands clamp to the floor, protected members of a crossing cohort get exactly zero consequences while unprotected members get step-up, the consequence floor still gates the new default, and IP alone - many identities, one address, no extraction behavior - creates no flag and no cohort).
- **Cursor V2 (`src/tier2-active/cursor-v2.ts`):** Added `mintCursorV2()` / `verifyCursorV2()` next to the unchanged V1 cursors. The V2 payload is allowlisted to position + subject/cohort/scope binding + `cursorSequence` + `ledgerVersion` - it never carries LLR or evidence snapshots (a signed token smuggling an extra field is rejected as `unexpected_fields`) - and verification checks the token against host-supplied store authority with the store winning unconditionally: `stale_version` and `future_version` are both rejected, never silently upgraded, and sequence mismatches reject chain replays. `createCursorV2Authority()` is a small in-memory authority for hosts not yet reading version/sequence from their own store. The accepted cost is stated in the module header: V2 pagination is not stateless, and a store outage fails new disclosure closed. Unit evidence in `tests/cursor-v2.test.cjs` (8 tests).
- **Evidence attribution rules (`src/tier2-active/evidence-attribution.ts`):** Added `createEvidenceAttributor()` implementing the CHATGPT-R8 poisoning defense: evidence credits the acting subject in full; cross-subject contribution is credited only over host-declared relationships, capped per pair and decayed on a configurable half-life; inferred relationships are observation-only (0 enforcement credit); unknown relationships are quarantined into a bounded audit log with 0 credit. Unit evidence in `tests/attribution-calibration.test.cjs`.
- **EvidenceReviewer hook (`src/tier2-active/evidence-reviewer.ts`):** Added the defender-agent idea's one promotable slice as an SDK interface: `createReviewerChannel()` emits bounded, aggregate-only `EvidenceBundle`s to a host-side reviewer and delivers back only schema-validated proposals from the fixed advisory vocabulary `REVIEWER_ACTIONS` (`no_action`, `request_step_up`, `request_human_review`, `suggest_observe_extension`, `suggest_exemption_review`). Enforcement-shaped output (a `deny` action, a `set_budget` field) is rejected whole. The channel holds no reference to any evidence engine and exposes exactly one method, so reviewer output architecturally cannot flow back into the calibrated LLR stream (which would double-count the observations it was derived from); a dedicated test wires the channel beside a live tripwire and proves its score and flag do not move. The autonomous defender agent itself remains LAB-ONLY and is not in this release. Unit evidence in `tests/reviewer-tiering.test.cjs`.
- **Suite:** 246 tests (244 pass, 2 pre-existing RSA-PSS skips, 0 fail), up from 180 in 2.3.0 - 66 new tests across the six v2.4 test files. New `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` rows state what the new modules do not claim, including the scripted-trace calibration (N_eff = 189), the tiling stream's inertness in the fitting harness, the still-open detail-channel cohort-formation gap, and the campaign ceiling's registry-completeness precondition.

## 2.3.0 — 2026-11-02

- **Data-economics package - distinct-record budget, export guard, pagination cursors (`src/tier2-active/record-budget.ts`, `export-guard.ts`, `cursor.ts`):** Added the server-side controls productized from the reconstruction-study lab (10,000-record target: an unprotected instance lost 100% of its dataset in 103 requests including a 1-request full export; the metered design capped extraction at exactly the configured budget, returned 0 export rows, rejected skip-ahead and stale-cursor probes, and left a polite human session with zero rejections). `createRecordBudget()` tracks how many DISTINCT records an identity (account > API key > IP, the quota guard's precedence) receives per window - the coverage dimension `createQuotaGuard` is memoryless about - with `check`/`consume`/`charge`, an Express middleware that consumes the ids a response actually contained via a host-supplied extractor, and `setOverride` for per-identity cap tightening. `createExportGuard()` rejects exports estimated above `maxRowsPerExport` with `422 export_scope_too_broad` before the handler runs, can require a narrowing filter parameter, and charges allowed exports against the record budget at a multiplier (default 2x) so the export channel is never a side door. `mintCursor()`/`verifyCursor()` implement session-chained pagination: HMAC-SHA256 tokens binding session, position and expiry, failing closed with distinct reasons (`bad_signature`, `expired`, `session_mismatch`, `position_mismatch`, `malformed`) for tampering, stale replay, cross-session replay and skip-ahead. All three are zero-dependency (Node builtins only), in-memory by default, O(1) on the normal path, and inert at human usage levels - the combined polite-human zero-friction gate is a unit test (`tests/detection-loop.test.cjs`), not an assertion. Unit evidence in `tests/record-budget.test.cjs`, `tests/export-guard.test.cjs`, `tests/cursor.test.cjs`. Honest scope, including the sybil dilution of any per-identity budget and the host-wiring dependence of the export row estimate, is in the new `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` rows.
- **Workflow-sequence flow scorer + decoy mirage - the detection-to-throttle loop (`src/tier2-active/flow-scorer.ts`, `decoy-mirage.ts`):** Added log-only sequence telemetry and an opt-in response loop on top of the data-economics package. `createFlowScorer()` scores per-session request SEQUENCES rather than individual requests - boundary probes (list requests rejected 429), post-429 persistence (the strongest signal in the study logs), sequential full-coverage pagination streaks, export bursts, and canary/decoy contact - emitting `onScore` at configurable elevated/high thresholds and never blocking, banning or altering a response itself. An `isExempt` hook is the verified-bot lane (Web Bot Auth verdicts, verified crawler rDNS); self-declared user agents are never exempted. `createDecoyMirage()` serves the deliberately unused routes a `200 OK` deterministic synthetic document (service-config / schema-registry / scoring-profile, seeded by path, byte-identical across calls and instances) instead of the canary `404`, under a strict safety subset: unused routes only, inert configuration-shaped content, synthetic data never mixed into real responses. The loop closes through an opt-in `onTaint` callback - fired on a high-threshold crossing or a canary/decoy contact - whose reference wiring lowers the tainted identity's record budget via `setOverride` until its window resets; other identities are untouched. Unit evidence in `tests/flow-scorer.test.cjs` (the study's agent sequence scores high with the expected reasons; a polite human sequence scores zero and emits nothing; exempt identities hold no state), `tests/decoy-mirage.test.cjs` (determinism, overrides, cross-site ignore), and `tests/detection-loop.test.cjs` (the full probe -> taint -> reduced-cap loop plus the polite-human gate). No effectiveness percentage is claimed - see the new `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` rows.
- **Hardening pass over the data-economics package (external red-team fixes):** `createRecordBudget` now prices records with a per-record state machine (viewed = 1, exported = 2, re-delivery free) via the new `consumeExported`, so view and export charges never stack on the same record; `createExportGuard` prices exports per-record when the host supplies `extractRecordIds` (the flat multiplier remains as the cruder estimate-only path), charges a `rejectionFloorUnits` floor on 422s, and both guards' middlewares set `Cache-Control: private, no-store` so metered responses cannot be replayed from cache (closing the cache-bypass accounting hole). The budget gained pre-flight `reserve`/`release` (middleware option `reserveUnits`) bounding parallel-burst overshoot to in-flight granularity, an `emptyResultFloorUnits` charge for zero-id responses (no free empty-result oracles), and bounded partitioned storage: record ids are stored as fixed-length FNV-1a hash keys, `ip:` identities live in a separate `maxIpEntries` pool that churn cannot use to evict account state, and per-identity stored keys cap at the effective limit + 1024. Taint hardening: `createFlowScorer` never fires `onTaint` for IP identities (score telemetry still fires) and only taints on `programmatic` decoy hits - `createDecoyMirage` now classifies every hit from Fetch Metadata (`hitKind: "ambient" | "programmatic"`) - and post-429 persistence only accrues when a post-429 attempt's signature differs from the rejected attempt, so SPA auto-retries no longer false-positive. The mirage gained `authorize` (plain 404, no hit), `validateRequest` (400, no hit) and `seedScope` (per-scope synthetic documents) hooks, with mounting behind the same auth as real routes documented as required. `verifyCursor`'s `expired` result now carries the decoded payload (signature-verified only) so hosts re-mint at the same position instead of 400ing a user with an old tab; all other failure reasons carry no payload fields. New unit evidence across `tests/record-budget.test.cjs`, `tests/export-guard.test.cjs`, `tests/cursor.test.cjs`, `tests/flow-scorer.test.cjs`, `tests/decoy-mirage.test.cjs` (suite: 152 tests). Residual limits - sybil economics and per-tier budget guidance, the residual reservation race, the memory-bound formula, decoy unmaskability by route-diffing - are stated in `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`.
- **Canary Maze (`src/tier2-active/honeypot-middleware.ts`):** Added opt-in `createCanaryMaze()` plus the `canaryTrapLink()` and `canaryRobotsTxt()` helpers. The maze serves a deterministic, seed-derived space of neutral wordlist-filler pages under a configurable prefix (default `/_canary/`): the same URL always renders the same page with no stored state, every page carries a `noindex,nofollow` meta, and every generated link stays inside the prefix, so no trap link can point at real content. Serving budgets are hard caps rather than tuning hints - a bounded per-IP window counter plus a global daily served-pages cap, after which the handler answers a plain 404 (or a configured 429) - so the trap cannot become a self-DDoS surface; an optional response drip defaults to off. Hits reuse the canary `onAlert` channel with two additive payload fields (`maze`, `depth`), and the alert semantics are unchanged: a hit is an investigation signal, never proof of malice and never an auto-ban. Content is neutral filler by design - no poisoned text, no payloads. Unit evidence (determinism, link containment, caps, kill switch, alert payload, trap-link and robots helpers) is in `tests/canary-maze.test.cjs`. Benchmark evidence, with full configs and raw logs in `benchmark/canary-maze/RESULTS.md`: Playwright + axe-core 4.14.0 found zero `aria-hidden-focusable` violations on a page carrying the bait link, the bait link never received keyboard focus in a 20-Tab traversal and was absent from the accessibility tree, and the generated maze page itself reports zero axe violations; wget 1.21.4 with default configuration made zero maze requests (it honored the robots.txt Disallow), while with `robots=off` it was served exactly the configured 30-page per-IP cap, then plain 404s, followed no link outside the prefix, and terminated on its own; direct requests to real paths were unaffected. That is one crawler, one run, on localhost - no effectiveness percentage is claimed - see the Canary Maze row in `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`.

- **Cross-identity herd detector + response ladder (`src/tier2-active/herd-detector.ts`):** Added `createHerdDetector()` and `applyHerdLadder()`, productized from the lab's cross-identity correlation chain (C-C6), which attacked the sybil dilution the record budget documents but cannot itself see: in the reconstruction study's round 3, one session extracted 100% of a 10,000-record dataset by rotating 6 free identities, each inside its own budget. The detector consumes the served-record stream incrementally (`observe` - signup/login/list/detail/export/page_view events) and groups identities two ways: grouping v1 chains signups within a window per source IP (the global cohort view is computed but diagnostic-only, as in the lab - its false-positive risk at real signup volume is unmeasurable in a lab), and grouping v2 links identities whose served-record sets are strongly complementary (pairwise Jaccard at most 0.10 over a union floor, co-active inside a rolling 7-day window) via union-find, which closes the aged-dispersed blind spot signup chaining is structurally blind to. Groups are scored on the lab's feature set (signup cluster, coverage ramp, tiling, contiguity, co-activity, cap pressure; the v2 score drops the cluster weight without renormalizing, matching the lab arithmetic) and flag once per group per window via `onFlag`. Lab evidence (scripted clients, 10,000-record target): fresh-chained herd flagged at 300 combined records and ladder-capped at 600; staggered herd 501; aged-bunched 300; aged-dispersed 2,400 by v2; dense legit onboarding team peaked at 47.2 of the 60 threshold with tiling exactly 0; shared-IP workday control never flagged. Every flag carries a response band - `budget_cut_supported` only at high tiling (the herd partition profile) - and `applyHerdLadder()` encodes the C6 lesson in code: it refuses low-tiling flags (`reason: "graduated_only"`, no override applied), because the one measured legitimate group over the threshold (a compliance team systematically reviewing a full segment, flagged at 60.008 with tiling 0.239) would otherwise have its budgets cut for doing its job; graduated responses (step-up verification, export-only restriction, human review) are the supported tier there. Record ids are stored as bounded FNV-1a hash keys with a hash-space bitmap pre-filter, following `createRecordBudget`'s storage approach. Unit evidence in `tests/herd-detector.test.cjs`: seven deterministic streams at 1,000-record scale reproducing the lab outcomes, including the combined dispersed+interleaved herd asserted as NOT flagged (peak 57.3 of 60 in the lab; the known evader is a documented limit, in test form). Honest scope - the interleaved+dispersed evader, micro-slice and shift-work herds as open shapes, the O(N^2) exact-pairwise scaling bound (honest to ~hundreds of concurrent identities; leader clustering named, not built), and the rule that every record-serving surface including server-rendered HTML must be metered and evented - is in the new `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` rows.
- **Round-4 blinded reconstruction test - the herd layer measured end-to-end:** The full stack (record budget, cursors, export guard, decoy + taint, herd detector + ladder, metered HTML routes) was wired from the built package into the study target and attacked by blinded independent agents (report: the study's `round4-results.md`). A REA-first session's identity rotation was flagged at 1,510 combined records (score 69.99, `budget_cut_supported`) and ladder-cut to 100 per member; its own extraction from the protected instance stopped at ~15% coverage — round 3's free-account sybil escape is closed for the high-tiling shape, and the unmetered-HTML escape is closed for the routes wired. An adaptive session rotating 18 identities with overlapped probing was flagged twice (1,311 and 5,999 combined records) but landed `graduated_only` both times, the ladder refused the cuts by design, and it extracted the full dataset in 272 requests: the enforcement ceiling is stated plainly in `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` — low-tiling herds are detected, not stopped, by this library; stopping them needs a host-side graduated response attached to the flag.
- **Independent-benchmark fix pass, part 1 - scanner correctness (GitHub issue #1):** `scripts/run-audit.cjs` no longer ignores its argument or depends on the caller's cwd: script paths resolve relative to the runner itself, a directory argument runs the build-directory scan against THAT directory (the Node scanner is now a full twin of `verify-build.py` with the same rules and report shape, exported as `scanArtifactDirectory` for tests), and no argument runs the repo self-check. (Previously the seven scan tests in `tests/scan.test.cjs` were silently inert — requiring the old runner exited the test process before any of them ran; they now execute for real.) In `scripts/verify-build.py`, an external `//# sourceMappingURL=` reference in JS/CSS is now a hard failure (exit 1) instead of a `review` note — it is the most common real leak and a CI gate previously passed it; the scanner also detects compressed map files (`.map.gz` / `.map.br`), source maps renamed to `.json` (sniffed for `mappings` + `sources` keys), `sourceMappingURL` inside `.svg` files, and `SourceMap:` response-header lines in `_headers` files. Files over 10 MB are scanned with a chunked marker search instead of being skipped, and the file cap (raised to 100,000) now emits an explicit fail-level `coverage-incomplete` finding rather than aborting the report. `scripts/` is included in the npm package `files`, so npm users receive the scanner. README test counts corrected to the real suite size.
- **Independent-benchmark fix pass, part 2 - fail-closed stores and quota identity (`src/tier2-active/quota-guard.ts`, `web-bot-auth.ts`, `src/tier3-crypto/transport-shield.ts`):** The bundled in-memory stores no longer evict unexpired entries when full. The quota window store evicts only expired windows and returns a refusal for a new window when still full, and `createQuotaGuard` then rejects the request (429, new kind `store_capacity_exceeded`, with an operator event) instead of silently weakening the guarantee; the Web Bot Auth nonce store and the transport-envelope replay guard fail closed the same way (a full replay guard rejects the envelope rather than forgetting a live nonce). `QuotaWindowStore.record` may now return `false` to signal refusal (existing stores returning nothing are unaffected). A quota request with no resolvable account, API key or IP is no longer exempt: it is counted against a single shared `unknown` bucket at the tier's normal limits by default, with the legacy skip available as the explicit `allowUnresolvedIdentity` option. The guard's documentation (module header and `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`) now states that hosts must consume the normalized pagination (`req.quotaPagination` / `result.pagination`) rather than re-reading raw query parameters, whose duplicate/array/case handling diverges across backends. Unit evidence in `tests/core.test.cjs` and `tests/web-bot-auth.test.cjs`.
- **Independent-benchmark fix pass, part 3 - verifier strictness and canary alert semantics (`src/tier2-active/web-bot-auth.ts`, `honeypot-middleware.ts`, `decoy-mirage.ts`):** The Web Bot Auth verifier now rejects duplicate covered components (new reason `duplicate_covered_components`; RFC 9421 §2.5 forbids them even when the signature verifies over the duplicated base), `expires` at or before `created` (new reason `invalid_validity_window`), and nonces longer than the new documented `MAX_NONCE_LENGTH` cap of 256 characters (new reason `nonce_too_long`) — all as clean verification failures, never throws. `ignoreCrossSite` now defaults to `false` in the canary trap, the Canary Maze and (for consistency) the decoy mirage: the `sec-fetch-site` header is client-supplied, so previously any non-browser client could opt itself out of detection by sending it; the option remains as an explicit noise heuristic for genuine browser cross-site embeds. Canary Maze alerts now fire AFTER the per-IP and daily cap checks and carry a `capped` boolean on the alert payload, so an alert always reflects the enforced outcome of the hit.

## 2.2.0 — 2026-11-01

- **Web Bot Auth verifier (`src/tier2-active/web-bot-auth.ts`):** Added `createWebBotAuthVerifier()` implementing the IETF Web Bot Auth profile (draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol) on RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures: Ed25519 verification of covered components, `keyid` bound to the RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, required `created`/`expires` with a capped validity window, and a bounded in-memory nonce replay guard. Keys resolve through a caller-injected resolver or a parsed signature-agent key directory (JWK Set shapes); the module performs no network fetching. A verified signature proves key possession for the covered request only - it is not authorization and not evidence of good behavior. Documented composition maps a verified verdict onto a caller-owned quota tier in `createQuotaGuard()` without changing quota-guard. 33 dedicated tests (real Ed25519 keys, tamper/expiry/replay cases). Interop is tested against the reference implementation: cross-signing with Cloudflare's `web-bot-auth` package passes in both directions and the IETF draft's published Ed25519 vector verifies (`tests/web-bot-auth-interop.test.cjs`, `scripts/interop-web-bot-auth.cjs`, weekly CI). Cloudflare's older architecture-v1 vectors exposed two profile divergences, each pinned by a named test with the reference signatures independently proven valid: requests without a `Signature-Agent` header are rejected (required by draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00 §5.2.1), and the legacy bare-string `Signature-Agent` form is handled by dual-form acceptance (below). **Dual-form `Signature-Agent` acceptance:** the verifier accepts both the draft dictionary form (`sig="https://..."`, the form -00 mandates for signers) and the legacy bare-string form (`Signature-Agent: "https://..."`). Rationale: the draft mandates the dictionary form, but Cloudflare's production verifier still requires the bare string and production signers send it deliberately, so a dictionary-only verifier would reject the deployed ecosystem; §5.2.1 expressly permits a verifier to accept the legacy form (MAY). The legacy form is a deprecated compatibility path, accepted only under a fail-closed guardrail (exactly one signature may cover the `signature-agent` field, via the whole-field component with no `;key` binding; ambiguous multi-signature coverage keeps being rejected), and every verdict reports the form used via the new additive `agentForm` field (`"dictionary"` | `"legacy"`) so operators can measure remaining legacy usage. Revisit this acceptance when the draft becomes an RFC or Cloudflare's production verifier flips to the dictionary form.
- **Python/FastAPI quota-guard port (`examples/python-fastapi/`):** Faithful port of `createQuotaGuard()` semantics to Python: identical tiers, sliding-window decisions, `429` + `Retry-After` / `X-RateLimit-*` wire format, and pagination bounds, with a `QuotaWindowStore` protocol (bounded in-memory implementation plus a Redis implementation against a duck-typed client via Lua scripts), a Starlette middleware, and FastAPI dependencies. 26 pytest parity tests mirror the TypeScript scenarios assertion-for-assertion; divergences (snake_case API, Starlette error path) are documented in the example README. The port is an example, not a published package. The Redis store is covered by unit tests against an in-memory fake plus real-Redis integration tests (gated by `REDIS_URL`) that also run in CI against a Redis service container; Redis failure modes and Cluster/Sentinel topologies remain untested and are documented as such in the example README.

Updated `.agents/skills/anti-rea/SKILL.md` to describe `signSvgPath` as a fragile provenance marker.

Restricted `/__benchmark/state` and `/__benchmark/reset` in `benchmark/demo/server.cjs` to loopback addresses, updated `configs/next.config.mjs` and `configs/vite.config.ts`, cited Vietnam's Decree 13/2023/ND-CP (PDPD) in `docs/LEGAL_PRIVACY.md`, and expanded unit test suite to 38 passing checks.
